channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: TikTok to Pay $400 Million to Settle DOJ Child Privacy Case
item.description: TikTok Inc. and Chinese parent ByteDance Ltd. agreed to pay $400 million to resolve a a Biden-era lawsuit by the Justice Department accusing the popular social media app of collecting data on children in violation of an online privacy law.
item.dc:creator: Josh Sisco and Alexandra S. Levine

item.title: Anthropic Taps Google Chip Veteran as Part of Push Into Hardware
item.description: Anthropic PBC has hired Amir Salek, a founder of the custom chip program at Alphabet Inc.’s Google, as the AI lab lays the groundwork for a push into making its own semiconductors.
item.dc:creator: Dina Bass

item.title: Ask Emily Chang About Interviewing Tech’s Biggest Names on The Circuit
item.description: Emily Chang interviews the top names in tech and business on The Circuit. Bring your questions and join her for an interactive Live Q&A conversation on Sept. 1 at 1 p.m. EDT
item.dc:creator: Emily Chang and Brad Stone

item.title: SpaceX Is Hiring in Natural Gas Trading for Energy Needs
item.description: Elon Musk’s SpaceX is hiring a trader to build and lead a natural gas trading team to support the space flight company’s growing fuel and power needs.
item.dc:creator: Julian Hast

item.title: Treasury Whiplash, US Debt Hits $40T | Bloomberg Money 8/21/2026
item.description: Bloomberg Money takes the pulse of your financial life, powered by the reporting of our global newsroom. Today's guests: Rebecca Patterson, Council on Foreign Relations Senior Fellow, and Kevin Gordon, Charles Schwab Head of Macro Research & Strategy. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Khosla Ventures Bets on AI’s Next Frontier: Science
item.description: Khosla Ventures is backing Discovery Loop, a new AI startup founded by former Google leaders including Jeff Dean that aims to dramatically accelerate scientific experimentation. Khosla Ventures Managing Director Samir Kaul explains why the firm quickly decided to invest, and why he believes the opportunity could be as profound as frontier AI models. He also discusses why soaring technology valuations are forcing venture investors to rethink what “seed stage” even means. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta Safety Trial Could Reveal What Zuckerberg, Others Knew
item.description: Meta is facing a landmark legal battle with 29 states accusing the company of deliberately designing its platforms to keep children hooked while misleading the public about their safety. George Washington University law professor Mary Anne Franks explains the state and federal claims, why the case has drawn comparisons to tobacco litigation, and why the biggest consequence may not be the potential financial penalty, but what internal documents reveal about what Meta knew and when. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Wall Street Struggles to Absorb AI’s Debt Boom
item.description: Broadcom is lining up another massive bet on AI. Bloomberg has learned the chipmaker is in talks to raise more than $60 billion in debt to help Anthropic and others secure chips and computing power. The deal highlights a bigger concern hanging over the AI trade: the cost of funding it all. Erica Klauer, Science and Technology Partners founder and CIO, discusses concerns around circular financing and why the AI buildout is so challenging. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Preps for Blockbuster Public Listing | Bloomberg Tech 8/21/2026
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow takes a look at Anthropic as the AI company expects to match or top the size of SpaceX's record-setting IPO. Plus, sources say Broadcom is in talks to raise more than $60 billion in debt to help Anthropic and others secure chips and computing power, and all eyes are on Nvidia as the chipmaker reports earnings next week. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Aims to Match or Top SpaceX IPO
item.description: Anthropic is aiming for an IPO that could make history, expecting to match or even top SpaceX's record-setting debut, according to sources. The maker of Claude could file publicly by the end of this month. The company raised $65 billion in May at a $965 billion valuation. Bloomberg's Shirin Ghaffary, who leads coverage of Anthropic, and Bloomberg's Liana Baker, who leads the deals team, join Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Robinhood's Guild on AI, Markets & Risks
item.description: Robinhood's Stephanie Guild discusses the impact of major AI IPOs, market concentration risks, opportunities in healthcare and compute infrastructure, and why investors should balance AI exposure with cash flow-focused, defensive assets. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple Cuts Jobs in Siri, Vision Pro Immersive Video and Gaming Teams
item.description: Apple Inc. is cutting jobs across teams responsible for the Siri digital assistant and the Vision Pro headset, part of an effort to focus on new devices and artificial intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gurman

item.title: Rockstar Rattled As ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ Leaks Again
item.description: After a leak in 2022 Rockstar took drastic measures to try to prevent another hack. It didn’t work.
item.dc:creator: Jason Schreier

item.title: The Stock Market’s Boom Will Likely Bust
item.description: It’s easy to make the case that the US equity market is in bubble territory when the major metrics point in the same direction. There are several reasons why this bubble will likely burst before the end of 2027. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Why Data Center Pushback Is a Unique Form of NIMBYism
item.description: Unlike solar farms or housing projects, data centers face a unique challenge: people don't just oppose them in their own backyards—they question if we need them at all. On Odd Lots, Jasmine Sun tells Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway why the AI industry and policymakers have failed to make a compelling case for the AI buildout, leading to widespread anxiety over resource usage. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Odd Lots: Why Many Communities Are Skeptical of the AI Boom
item.description: From electrical contractors to HVAC engineers, people far from Silicon Valley are quietly asking the same question: Is AI a bubble? Speaking with Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway on Odd Lots, Jasmine Sun explains how local communities weigh the massive economic tradeoffs of multi-year data center projects when they aren't even sure if the technology—or its funding—is here to stay. Listen wherever you get your podcasts. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apollo Reports Data Breach From ‘Social Engineering Incident’
item.description: Apollo Global Management Inc. said hackers breached its systems in July and accessed personal information, following a spate of attempted or successful cyberattacks at major hedge funds in recent weeks.
item.dc:creator: Laura Benitez

item.title: Uber Faces €825 Million Dutch Fine Over Driver Suspensions
item.description: Uber Technologies Inc. has been fined €825 million ($963 million) by Dutch authorities for using automated systems to suspend driver accounts, in what is the second-largest penalty under the European Union’s General Data Protection Regulation.
item.dc:creator: Charlotte Hughes-Morgan

item.title: UK Bets on a Boom in AI Chip Newcomers
item.description: The government is helping fund some promising startups to gain a domestic foothold in the industry
item.dc:creator: Mark Bergen

item.title: Nvidia to Pay AI Startup Poolside a $6 Billion License, Newcomer Says
item.description: Nvidia Corp. has agreed to pay $6 billion to license artificial intelligence models from Poolside and will extend job offers to more than 100 employees, according to people familiar with the situation.
item.dc:creator: Benoit Berthelot, Rebecca Torrence and Ian King
